what_its_for: Cimetidine is used to treat heartburn, acid indigestion, and sour stomach. It is also used to treat and prevent ulcers in the stomach and small intestine, and to treat conditions where the stomach makes too much acid (such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome). It works by reducing the amount of acid your stomach produces.
how_to_take: Take cimetidine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. If you are using it for heartburn, you may take it right before or up to 30 minutes before eating a meal or drinking a beverage that causes you heartburn. Do not take more than directed on the package or by your doctor. If you are taking antacids, try to take them at a different time than cimetidine, as antacids can make it harder for your body to absorb cimetidine.
dosing: For over-the-counter heartburn relief in adults and children 12 years and older: the usual dose is 200 mg (one tablet) taken once or twice a day with water. Do not take more than 400 mg (two tablets) in 24 hours, and do not use for more than 14 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to. For prescription use, your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take and when, as doses can vary depending on your condition. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cimetidine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cimetidine, as it can increase stomach acid and make your symptoms worse. Avoid smoking, as it can also increase stomach acid and slow healing of ulcers. Avoid taking cimetidine at the same time as antacids — space them apart by at least 1 hour. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, as cimetidine can interact with many drugs including blood thinners (like warfarin), certain heart medications, seizure medications, and some antidepressants. Avoid taking more than the recommended dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: trouble swallowing or painful swallowing, vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, bloody or black tarry stools, chest pain or tightness, severe stomach pain, unexplained weight loss, or if your heartburn has lasted more than 3 months. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after 14 days of use, or if they get worse. Seek immediate help if you have signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Cimetidine usually starts to relieve heartburn symptoms within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking it. For ulcer healing, it may take several weeks of regular use before you feel full benefit. Continue taking it for as long as your doctor has prescribed, even if you start feeling better sooner.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of cimetidine and may have a higher risk of side effects such as confusion or dizziness. A lower dose may be recommended. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, talk to your doctor before using cimetidine. Your dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using cimetidine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Cimetidine can pass into breast milk. Children: Over-the-counter cimetidine is not recommended for children under 12 years old unless directed by a doctor.
